newsitem.title: USA: US border officials chide Mexico on bogus documents.
newsitem.headline: US border officials chide Mexico on bogus documents.

text.p: Immigration officials criticised Mexico's government on Wednesday for allegedly failing to crack down on counterfeiters who forge documents allowing illegal immigrants to cross into the United States.

Dan Kane, a U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service spokesman in El Paso, said the U.S.-Mexico border is being "flooded" with false documents and that nothing is being done on the other side of the border to stop it, despite appeals to Mexico's federal government and police forces.
"It's proliferating without any challenge from Mexican law enforcement," Kane told Reuters. "The Mexican government does not seem to care about these false Mexican documents."
Bogus Mexican and U.S. passports, border crossing cards and residency cards are commonly used by illegal immigrants trying to get across the border.
INS officials say about 11,000 false documents have been seized in the past six months in west Texas and New Mexico alone. Of those, 7,000 were false Mexican documents.
But Mexican officials said Kane's criticisms were unjustified.

"That is an unfair statement. They didn't give (Mexican police) enough time to take appropriate action," said Manuel Hernandez, a spokesman for the Mexican consulate in El Paso. He declined to comment further "because we would start unnecessary tensions."

Apart from the professional counterfeiters, Kane said some Mexican citizens are also selling their legitimate documents for about $400 each to illegal immigrants who superimpose their own pictures on top of the original.
He said thousands of people report their documents stolen and receive a replacement, but it is often hard to tell whether the originals were lost or sold.
